verdict.rationale: Claude Code's own docs give leads two levers: managed policy settings for organization-wide configuration (Enterprise), and a Bash sandbox where you define which network domains commands can reach, with OS enforcement. External integrations are attached explicitly via `claude mcp add`. However, no evidence describes per-tool or per-MCP-server allow/deny lists, or exactly what managed policies can restrict. Missing for 10: documented per-tool/MCP-server allowlists or denylists, detail on which integrations managed policy settings can restrict, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can control which external tools and integrations the agent is allowed to access

citations.quote: managed policy settings for organization-wide Claude Code configurations
you define which files and network domains commands can touch, and the operating system enforces that boundary for every Bash command and its child processes
claude mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
